key_insight: The paper argues that scientific ideas evolve like genomes: new work is built by inheriting, repairing, and recombining parts of prior research. To test whether AI can reason about this lineage, the authors introduce IG-Bench, a benchmark focused on scientific inheritance and idea generation.
problem_solved: Current AI benchmarks do not adequately measure whether models can trace how scientific ideas derive from earlier papers or generate new ideas grounded in that lineage. This paper addresses the gap between generic reasoning benchmarks and the real structure of scientific innovation.
method: Introduces IdeaGene-Bench (IG-Bench), a benchmark for scientific lineage reasoning and lineage-grounded idea generation.
Organizes papers and proposals using the IdeaGene framework, representing each as a set of minimal inherited components.
Evaluates whether AI systems can identify lineage relationships and produce new ideas that correctly build on prior mechanisms and limitations.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this benchmark provides a more realistic way to assess research-assistant models, literature reasoning systems, and idea-generation tools. It encourages systems that do not just summarize papers, but understand how scientific ideas evolve and can responsibly extend them.
visual_elements: A genome-like diagram showing idea inheritance, mutation, and recombination across papers
A pipeline graphic from prior work -> limitation -> repair -> new proposal
A benchmark overview chart showing lineage reasoning vs. lineage-grounded generation tasks
Icon set for mechanisms, gaps, recombination, and evaluation
paper_title: Ideas Have Genomes: Benchmarking Scientific Lineage Reasoning and Lineage-Grounded Idea Generation
paper_authors: Yifan Zhou, Qihao Yang, Yan Li, Donggang Li, Xiru Hu
